intro: On the Asian shore of the Bosphorus, in İstanbul province, stands Beylerbeyi Palace, built in 1861–1865. This was the summer palace of Sultan Abdülaziz, and it was used to house visiting heads of state. It also saw a quieter ending: Abdülhamid II died here under house arrest.
history: Sultan Abdülaziz had Sarkis Balyan build this summer palace between 1861 and 1865, in place of a wooden kiosk. It was used to receive visiting heads of state, and the Empress Eugénie of France and the Shah of Persia both stayed here. Then the story turns. After his deposition, Abdülhamid II spent his last six years in this palace, under house arrest.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the pool hall and the blue hall, the seaside kiosks, and the yellow kiosk with its terraced gardens.
facts: Did you know? Egyptian reed matting covers the floors of the halls, chosen to keep the rooms cool in the damp air off the Bosphorus. And the palace was used to receive heads of state: the Empress Eugénie of France and the Shah of Persia both stayed here.
outro: This brings our tour of Beylerbeyi Palace to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Royal guests once passed through these halls; let them welcome those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
